r0.why: Colloquial term, photosynthetic single cells, symbiosis with corals, jellyfish, demosponges, nudibranchs [1]; Symbiodinium, Amphidinium, unidentified taxa [2]; 'little yellow animal', Karl Brandt 1881 [3].

r1.why: Daytime photosynthetic products, up to 90% of energy for metabolism, growth, reproduction [6]; nutrients, CO2, raised sunlit position in return [7]; reef corals, sea anemones, giant clam, flatworms [45].

r2.why: Taken up by host lysosomes [22]; not degraded because they provided carbon compounds [23]; chlorophyll a/c, peridinin, diadinoxanthin giving yellowish/brownish host colours [5], following the source's own grouping.

r3.why: Thylakoids in threes [10]; pyrenoid with thick starchy covering [11]; tightly compacted chromatin in nucleus [17,18]; 5-hydroxymethyluracil and thymidine unlike other eukaryotes [21].

r4.why: Cysts and motile phases [24]; vegetative predominant, thin wall, divides or becomes cyst [29,30,33]; cysts thick-walled, majority, reddish-brown [35,36]; dividing cysts a fourth, daughters adjoined [37].

r5.why: Zoosporangium/zoospore stages much rarer [39]; zoosporangium matures to motile zoospore [27]; only motile if from zoospore [41]; forward rotation on posterior flagellum or gyration attached to substrate [42-44]; releases gametes [28].
